name: Historic City of Ahmadabad
description: Founded in 1411 by Sultan Ahmad Shah on the east bank of the Sabarmati river in Gujarat, India, Ahmadabad's walled old city is a dense maze of sultanate-era mosques, tombs, gateways and the Bhadra citadel. Wander its gated residential lanes, called pols, where wooden houses cluster around public wells and ornate bird feeders. Hindu and Jain temples sit alongside, in a city that has stayed Gujarat's capital for six centuries.
